description: Add the explicit STATED retention-and-redaction policy required by scope note sections 1 and 6, and verify the code's behavior matches it. The redaction-before-storage behavior already exists (services/extraction.py masks emails/phones/roll numbers/names; the pipeline only ever returns and persists redacted_text + extracted fields; the Notice model has no unredacted-original column). What is MISSING is the explicit stated policy in the specs and docs. The policy must state, in scope-note language: personal identifiers (names, roll numbers, contact details) are redacted at ingestion before the notice is stored or indexed; the unredacted original is NOT retained; raw fetched files are kept only for the duration of project evaluation; and the benchmark released with the report contains redacted text only. Add this to requirements.md and design.md and README.md. Also verify (do not merely assert) that the unredacted original is never persisted.
steps: Read services/extraction.py (redact(), extract()), services/ingestion.py (upsert_official, create_submission, _apply_extraction), and models.py (the Notice model fields) to confirm no unredacted-original column exists and only redacted_text is stored. Also confirm extraction.extract() returns only redacted_text + fields and fields are parsed from the redacted text.

Add a clear 'Data handling and retention' policy statement. In requirements.md: add explicit retention wording to the R2 (Extraction) section or a dedicated subsection under GC-5/R2.3/R2.4, stating: identifiers (names, roll numbers, contact details) are redacted at ingestion before storage/indexing; the unredacted original is NOT retained; raw fetched files are kept only for the duration of project evaluation; the released benchmark contains redacted text only. Keep EARS phrasing where appropriate (e.g. 'The system SHALL NOT retain the unredacted original.').

In design.md: extend the redaction description (section 5, module 2 / extraction) with a short 'Retention policy' note reflecting the same four points and referencing that the Notice table stores only redacted_text (no unredacted column) so the policy is enforced structurally, not just procedurally.

In README.md: add a short 'Data handling and retention' subsection (near the OCR/Tesseract note or the extraction bullet) stating the same policy in plain language so a reader/professor sees it up front.

Verify the code matches the stated policy: add or extend a backend test (tests/test_extraction.py or tests/test_ingestion.py) proving that after ingesting a notice containing PII (email/phone/roll/name), the PERSISTED notice.redacted_text and all stored NoticeField values contain the redaction masks and NOT the original PII, and that there is no attribute/column on the persisted Notice holding the unredacted original. This is a behavioral check that would fail if an unredacted original were ever stored.
Run the full backend test suite to confirm green.
acceptance_criteria: requirements.md, design.md, and README.md each contain an explicit, stated retention-and-redaction policy covering: redaction-before-storage of identifiers, unredacted original NOT retained, raw fetched files kept only for the duration of project evaluation, benchmark released contains redacted text only.

A backend test verifies that a persisted notice ingested from PII-containing text stores only redacted text/fields (masks present, original PII absent) and holds no unredacted original - and would fail if an unredacted original were persisted.
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m pytest finalsay/tests -q passes all tests.
verification: cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m pytest finalsay/tests/test_extraction.py finalsay/tests/test_ingestion.py -q  (all pass, including the new retention/redaction persistence check)
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m pytest finalsay/tests -q  (full suite passes)
grep the three docs to confirm the retention policy statement is present in requirements.md, design.md, and README.md
findings:
Stated the retention-and-redaction policy (scope note s1,s6) in all three docs and added a behavioral persistence test. All acceptance criteria met; committed as b1e454f on work/finalsay-prototype.

CODE CONFIRMATION (verify, not assert): models.py Notice has redacted_text (Text) and NO unredacted-original column; extraction.extract() runs redact() first then extract_fields() over the REDACTED text and returns only ExtractionResult(redacted_text, fields); ingestion _apply_extraction/_store_fields persist only redacted_text + parsed fields. The structural guarantee holds.

WHAT CHANGED (4 files):
- requirements.md: added subsection 'Data handling and retention policy (scope note s1, s6)' under section 2 (Extraction) with EARS reqs R2.5-R2.8: identifiers redacted at ingestion before storage/indexing; SHALL NOT retain the unredacted original (structural, no unredacted column); raw fetched files kept only for the duration of project evaluation; released benchmark contains redacted text only.
- design.md: added a 'Retention policy (scope note s1, s6)' note to section 5 (Extraction, module 2) covering the same four points and referencing that the notice table stores only redacted_text (no unredacted column, see s3) so the policy is enforced structurally.
- README.md: added a 'Data handling and retention' subsection after the OCR/Tesseract note, in plain language, covering all four points.
- backend/finalsay/tests/test_ingestion.py: added two BEHAVIORAL tests. test_persisted_submission_holds_only_redacted_text_no_unredacted_original persists a PII notice via ingestion.create_submission, commits, expunge_all(), re-reads from the DB, and asserts (a) redacted_text has masks and none of the 5 original PII strings, (b) no persisted Notice string attribute contains any original PII, (c) the Notice table has no unredacted-original-named column, (d) every stored NoticeField value is PII-free. test_persisted_official_holds_only_redacted_text does the same via the upsert_official path. Imported NoticeField.

TEETH CHECK: temporarily monkeypatched extraction.redact to identity (in-process only, no source change) and confirmed the new test FAILS with the original email leaking into notice.redacted_text - proving the test would fail if an unredacted original were ever persisted. Reverted (nothing written to source).

VERIFICATION (all green):
- pytest finalsay/tests/test_extraction.py finalsay/tests/test_ingestion.py -q: passed (15, +2).
- pytest finalsay/tests: 57 passed (was 55, +2).
- grep confirms the retention statement (unredacted original not retained / duration of project evaluation / benchmark contains redacted text only) is present in requirements.md, design.md, and README.md.

AUTONOMOUS DECISIONS:
- Put the behavioral test in test_ingestion.py (not test_extraction.py) because it must actually persist + re-read a notice, and test_ingestion.py already has the db_session fixture and ingestion-service pattern; extraction tests are unit-level on the pipeline.
- Committed ONLY the four FEAT-003 files. The uncommitted dataset.py/seed.py/test_seed.py are FEAT-001's changes, which the briefing/FEAT-001 findings say were intentionally left uncommitted on this branch; did not touch or commit them. Left tree committable, did not push or open a PR.
- Avoided em dashes in authored doc content (removed one from the design.md note).
- HANDOFF.md not updated here (flagged in context.json as a whole-pass deliverable; left for the orchestrator / a dedicated feature, consistent with FEAT-001/002).

V1-REVIEW REFINEMENT (wording-only, coverage not weakened): the v1 semantic review (APPROVED) noted R2.7's SHALL/active-voice wording implied a runtime deletion guarantee with no enforcing code path. Softened R2.7 in requirements.md, the section 5 note in design.md, and the 'Data handling and retention' subsection in README.md so the raw-fetched-files retention window reads as a STATED operational policy/intent (explicitly noting the prototype has no automated deletion/expiry path and enforcement is operational). All four scope-note points remain present in all three docs; the other three points (redaction-before-storage, unredacted original not retained, benchmark redacted-only) were left unchanged. 57 tests still pass.
